practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following founded the independent state of Hyderabad in the Deccan?
practiceQuestions.sol: Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I (Chin Qilich Khan) founded the independent state of Hyderabad in 1724, taking advantage of the decline of the Mughal Empire after Aurangzeb's death. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the original personal name of Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I?
practiceQuestions.sol: Mir Qamar-ud-Din Khan was the original birth name of Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I, while 'Chin Qilich Khan' and 'Nizam-ul-Mulk' were titles bestowed upon him by Mughal Emperors. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India: From Sultanat to the Mughals]

practiceQuestions.q: In which year was the Treaty of Mungi Patan signed between the Marathas and Nizam-ul-Mulk?
practiceQuestions.sol: Following his defeat at the Battle of Palkhed (1728) by Peshwa Baji Rao I, Nizam-ul-Mulk was forced to sign the Treaty of Mungi Patan in March 1728. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Historical Textbooks]

practiceQuestions.q: Which battle fought in 1728 established the military superiority of Peshwa Baji Rao I over Nizam-ul-Mulk?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Battle of Palkhed (1728) showcased Baji Rao I's mastery over guerrilla warfare and mobility, completely outmaneuvering the Nizam and forcing a humiliating treaty. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra, History of Modern India / Standard Historical Canon]

practiceQuestions.q: The Battle of Shakarkhera (1724) was fought between Nizam-ul-Mulk and whom?
practiceQuestions.sol: Mubariz Khan, the loyal Mughal governor of Hyderabad who opposed Nizam's assertion of autonomy, was defeated and killed by Nizam-ul-Mulk at the Battle of Shakarkhera in October 1724. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which treaty was signed in 1738 following the Nizam's defeat at the Battle of Bhopal by the Marathas?
practiceQuestions.sol: After being besieged at Bhopal in 1738, the Nizam signed the Convention of Duraha, ceding Malwa and promising a massive indemnity to the Marathas. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History Resources]

practiceQuestions.q: The famous Battle of Udgir (1760) was fought between the Marathas and which representative of the Nizam?
practiceQuestions.sol: Led by Sadashivrao Bhau, the Marathas decisively defeated Salabat Jung's forces at the Battle of Udgir (1760), forcing the Nizam to surrender vast territories including Ahmednagar, Bijapur, and parts of Bidar. [Primary Reference: Advanced Study in the History of Modern India, Jaswant Lal Mehta]

practiceQuestions.q: Which Mughal Emperor conferred the title 'Asaf Jah' upon Nizam-ul-Mulk?
practiceQuestions.sol: Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah bestowed the high-ranking title 'Asaf Jah' on Nizam-ul-Mulk in 1725, recognizing his de facto control over the Deccan provinces. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: In the administrative structure of the Deccan under the Nizam, what was the primary role of the 'Diwan'?
opts: Head of revenue and finance department
practiceQuestions.sol: The Diwan served as the prime minister and head of the financial administration in the Nizam's state, managing revenue collections and state expenditures. [Primary Reference: Imperial Gazetteer of India / Historical Administrative Manuals]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following revenue rights did the Marathas consistently demand from the Nizam over Mughal territories in the Deccan?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Marathas continuously asserted their claim to collect Chauth (25%) and Sardeshmukhi (10%) from the six Mughal provinces of the Deccan, which became a major bone of contention with the Nizam. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/12 History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the political relationship between Nizam-ul-Mulk and the rising Maratha Confederacy reflect the wider crisis of the Mughal Empire?
opts: It showed a united front of regional powers against European expansionism in coastal India.
It illustrated the fragmentation of imperial authority where regional satraps and indigenous forces competed for surplus agrarian revenue.
It proved the complete military resurgence of central Mughal control under provincial Viceroys.
It resulted in the immediate elimination of feudal land tenure across the Deccan plateau.
practiceQuestions.sol: The struggle between the Nizam and the Marathas highlights how regional governors (subahdars) carved out autonomous spheres while indigenous powers like the Marathas extracted revenue concessions (Chauth/Sardeshmukhi), marking the collapse of centralized Mughal fiscal administration. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was Nizam-ul-Mulk's core geopolitical strategy when dealing with the internal succession disputes of the Maratha Confederacy (such as between Shahu and Tarabai or later Peshwa rivalries)?
opts: Unconditional military backing of Shahu to maintain permanent imperial peace.
Playing off rival factions against each other ('divide and rule') to prevent a consolidated Maratha threat on Hyderabad's borders.
Directly annexing Satara and Kolhapur into the direct administrative control of Hyderabad.
Completely ignoring Maratha politics and focusing exclusively on northern Mughal courts.
practiceQuestions.sol: Nizam-ul-Mulk frequently exploited internal Maratha divisions (supporting Sambhaji II of Kolhapur against Shahu) to weaken their cohesive pressure on his newly formed Hyderabad state, exemplifying classic balance-of-power diplomacy. [Primary Reference: NCERT History / Modern Indian History Canonical Studies]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did the Marathas under Baji Rao I prefer extracting Chauth rather than direct annexation and direct administration of the Deccan provinces under the Nizam?
opts: They lacked the administrative machinery and manpower to govern vast settled agricultural tracts directly while pursuing northern expansion.
The Mughal Emperor strictly prohibited Maratha direct rule under imperial fatwas.
Direct taxation generated far less revenue than arbitrary plunder.
Nizam-ul-Mulk had nuclear military superiority that prevented any territorial acquisition.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Maratha fiscal strategy under the Peshwas relied on monetizing tributary claims (Chauth and Sardeshmukhi) because maintaining direct administrative control over hostile, distant provinces required immense garrison costs, whereas tribute provided steady cash flow with minimal administrative overhead. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra, History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Nizam-ul-Mulk utilize his position as Wazir of the Mughal Empire (1737-1740) vis-à-vis the expanding Maratha power?
opts: He successfully mobilized the combined resources of the entire Mughal Empire to permanently crush the Marathas at Delhi.
He went to Delhi to counter the growing influence of the Iran-Turan factions, but failed to stop Baji Rao's raid on Delhi and suffered defeat at Bhopal.
He formally ceded all territories of Northern India to the Marathas in exchange for safe passage to Hyderabad.
He merged the Maratha Confederacy directly into the Mughal imperial cabinet.
practiceQuestions.sol: Called to Delhi to save the decaying Mughal Empire, Nizam-ul-Mulk found himself powerless against Baji Rao I, whose lightning strike on Delhi (1737) and subsequent defeat of the Nizam at Bhopal (1738) exposed the utter bankruptcy of Mughal central authority. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: In the comparative evolution of regional states post-Aurangzeb, how did Hyderabad under the Nizam differ fundamentally from the Maratha Confederacy?
opts: Hyderabad maintained a centralized, bureaucratic administrative structure modeled closely on Mughal lines, whereas the Marathas evolved into a decentralized confederacy of autonomous chiefs.
Hyderabad practiced pure democratic governance while the Marathas operated a rigid religious autocracy.
The Nizam rejected all Islamic administrative titles, whereas the Marathas fully adopted Persian court culture.
Hyderabad was based entirely on maritime trade, while the Marathas relied solely on pastoral nomadism.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Nizam's state was an autocratic successor state that preserved traditional Mughal administrative machinery (mansabdari, jagirdari, subahdari), whereas the Maratha state transformed from a centralized swarajya under Shivaji into a sprawling confederacy held together by tributary hegemony and military dynamism. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History]

practiceQuestions.q: What role did European powers (especially the French and English East India Companies) play in the later conflicts between the Marathas and the Nizams after the death of Nizam-ul-Mulk in 1748?
opts: They remained completely neutral and banned their mercenaries from participating in Deccan wars.
They intervened in succession disputes (Carnatic/Hyderabad wars), providing disciplined infantry and artillery in exchange for territorial cessions, thus altering the native balance of power.
They conquered both Hyderabad and Pune, establishing direct colonial rule in 1750.
They acted as tax collectors for both the Marathas and the Nizam.
practiceQuestions.sol: Following Asaf Jah I's death, civil wars erupted in Hyderabad (Nasir Jung vs. Muzaffar Jung/Salabat Jung). French general Bussy stationed troops in Hyderabad in exchange for the Northern Circars, introducing European military technology and political meddling that permanently altered Maratha-Nizam dynamics. [Primary Reference: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the geographic configuration of the Deccan plateau influence the military strategy of the Marathas against the Nizam?
opts: It forced the Marathas to rely solely on heavy European-style siege artillery.
The rugged terrain, hills, and river valleys favored Maratha light cavalry and guerrilla tactics (Ganimi Kawa), allowing them to exhaust slow-moving Mughal-style imperial armies.
It made military movement impossible for nine months of the year.
It required naval blockades along the Godavari river.
practiceQuestions.sol: The terrain of the Deccan was ideally suited for Maratha light cavalry warfare. By avoiding pitched battles and cutting off supply lines (as seen at Palkhed and Bhopal), the Marathas exploited geography to neutralize the Nizam's superior artillery and heavy cavalry. [Primary Reference: Jadunath Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the broader economic impact of the perpetual warfare between the Marathas and Nizam-ul-Mulk on the Deccan peasantry?
opts: It led to agricultural prosperity and technological innovation in irrigation.
Double taxation (Chauth demanded by Marathas and land revenue by Nizam's officials) along with military plunder devastated rural agriculture and depopulated villages.
Peasants were exempted from all taxes during the continuous wars.
It stimulated a massive industrial revolution in textile manufacturing across Hyderabad.
practiceQuestions.sol: The extraction of Chauth and Sardeshmukhi by Maratha tax-gatherers (Golkhandas/Kamavisdars) on top of the regular revenue demands of the Nizam's administration resulted in severe economic exploitation, rural distress, and flight of peasantry from the contested zones. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Nizam-ul-Mulk manage relations with local Hindu zamindars and deshmukhs in his efforts to consolidate the Hyderabad state?
opts: He completely liquidated all Hindu landlords and replaced them exclusively with Turani nobles.
He adopted a pragmatic policy of accommodation, employing Hindu revenue officials (Kayasths and Khatris) and partnering with local landed elites to ensure stable tax collection.
He forced all local elites to convert to Islam under state decree.
He handed over all administrative offices to Maratha Brahman generals.
practiceQuestions.sol: Nizam-ul-Mulk was politically astute; while maintaining an Islamic administrative umbrella, he heavily relied on Hindu administrative talent (especially Kayasths in revenue management) and worked alongside local deshmukhs to maintain order and tax flows, demonstrating realpolitik. [Primary Reference: Karen Leonard, Hyderabad: The Political System]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the ultimate geopolitical significance of the long-standing Maratha-Nizam rivalry on the eve of the Third Battle of Panipat (1761)?
opts: The Nizam completely allied with the Marathas to defeat Ahmad Shah Abdali.
The exhaustion of Maratha-Nizam conflicts left the Deccan politically unstable and prevented a united indigenous front against external invaders or British colonial expansion.
It led to the complete dissolution of the Hyderabad state and absorption into the Maratha Empire.
It resulted in a permanent peace treaty brokered by the British East India Company.
practiceQuestions.sol: Decades of destructive rivalry between the Marathas and the Nizam prevented any coherent pan-Deccan coalition. Even during the crisis of Abdali's invasion, mutual distrust persisted (e.g., Nizam's forces testing Maratha vulnerability at Udgir just prior to Panipat), weakening Indian political resilience. [Primary Reference: Jadunath Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I:
1. He served as the Subahdar of the Deccan twice under the Mughal emperors before establishing his independent rule in 1724.
2. He strongly supported the Sayyid Brothers in overthrowing Farrukhsiyar to consolidate his absolute power at Delhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Nizam-ul-Mulk served as Deccan Viceroy from 1713-1715 and again was appointed in 1720 before firmly carving out Hyderabad in 1724. Statement 2 is incorrect: Nizam-ul-Mulk was a prominent opponent of the Sayyid Brothers (the 'Kingmakers'), allying instead with Muhammad Shah and the Turani faction to eliminate their influence. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Palkhed (1728):
1. It was fought between Peshwa Baji Rao I and Nizam-ul-Mulk.
2. The battle demonstrated the tactical superiority of traditional Mughal heavy artillery over Maratha light cavalry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Battle of Palkhed was fought in February-March 1728 between Baji Rao I and Nizam-ul-Mulk. Statement 2 is incorrect: The battle actually proved the exact opposite—Baji Rao's lightning mobility, cutting off supplies and encircling the Nizam, completely paralyzed the Nizam's heavy artillery and forces, resulting in a humiliating defeat. [Primary Reference: NCERT History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the revenue extraction system known as Chauth and Sardeshmukhi:
1. Chauth amounted to 25 percent of the standard revenue claimed from Mughal territories, given in lieu of protection against plunder.
2. Sardeshmukhi was an additional 10 percent levy claimed by the Maratha ruler as the hereditary chief deshmukh of the Deccan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Chauth was 25% of the land revenue exacted to prevent Maratha raids, while Sardeshmukhi was an extra 10% collected by the Maratha king based on his historical claim of being the 'Sardeshmukh' (overlord deshmukh) of Maharashtra. Both formed the cornerstone of Maratha fiscal imperialism over Nizam's territories. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Treaty of Mungi Patan (1728):
1. It was signed between Peshwa Baji Rao I and Nizam-ul-Mulk following the Battle of Palkhed.
2. Under this treaty, the Nizam recognized Shahu as the rightful Maratha Chhatrapati and agreed to pay arrears of Chauth and Sardeshmukhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Treaty of Mungi Patan formalized the Nizam's defeat at Palkhed, obligating him to acknowledge Shahu's rights to Chauth and Sardeshmukhi across the six subahs of the Deccan and to cease supporting rival Maratha factions. [Primary Reference: Jaswant Lal Mehta, Advanced Study in the History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Bhopal (1738):
1. The Nizam was besieged at Bhopal by Maratha forces led by Baji Rao I.
2. The conflict resulted in the total annexation of Hyderabad state into the Maratha Empire.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Baji Rao besieged the Nizam at Bhopal in late 1738. Statement 2 is incorrect: Hyderabad was not annexed; rather, the Nizam signed the Convention of Duraha, ceding Malwa and promising 50 lakh rupees as indemnity to the Marathas while retaining his autonomous state. [Primary Reference: NCERT History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the administrative machinery of Hyderabad established by Nizam-ul-Mulk:
1. He completely abolished the Mughal Mansabdari and Jagirdari systems within his territories to prevent external interference.
2. He maintained strict personal supervision over revenue administration and curbed the power of corrupt tax-farmers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Nizam preserved the traditional Mughal administrative framework, including mansabdari and jagirdari systems, adapting them to his autonomous state. Statement 2 is correct: Nizam-ul-Mulk instituted rigorous administrative checks, curbed corruption among revenue officials, and re-established order in agrarian tax collection. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the geopolitical context of the Deccan post-1748:
1. The death of Nizam-ul-Mulk in 1748 plunged Hyderabad into civil wars of succession involving French and British interventions.
2. The Marathas completely refrained from interfering in Hyderabad's succession disputes due to a formal non-aggression pact.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Asaf Jah I's death initiated violent succession struggles (Nasir Jung vs Muzaffar Jung), paving the way for European proxy involvement. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Marathas actively intervened in these succession disputes to extract massive territorial and financial concessions (such as during the battles leading to Udgir). [Primary Reference: Spectrum, Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Udgir (1760):
1. It was fought between the Marathas under Sadashivrao Bhau and the forces of the Nizam represented by Salabat Jung.
2. The victory enabled the Marathas to acquire major forts and territories including Ahmednagar and Bijapur.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. In 1760, Sadashivrao Bhau decisively defeated the Nizam's forces at Udgir, compelling the Hyderabad state to surrender vast territories, yielding immense strategic advantage to the Marathas just prior to the Panipat campaign. [Primary Reference: Jaswant Lal Mehta, Advanced Study in the History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the interaction of Nizam-ul-Mulk with European trading companies:
1. He encouraged the expansion of English and French trading outposts along the Coromandel coast to generate custom duties for his treasury.
2. He successfully expelled all European military adventurers from the Deccan throughout his lifetime.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Nizam recognized the economic vitality of maritime trade along the Coromandel coast and derived customs revenue from European factories. Statement 2 is incorrect: While Asaf Jah I kept European military intervention strictly contained during his lifetime, he did not expel them; rather, deep European military intervention (like Bussy's deployment) began only *after* his death in 1748. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing the Maratha Confederacy and Hyderabad under the Nizam:
1. While Hyderabad was unified under the hereditary dynastic rule of the Asaf Jahi family, the Maratha polity evolved into a confederacy headed by semi-autonomous chiefs like the Scindias, Holkars, and Gaekwads.
2. Both states completely rejected the nominal suzerainty of the Mughal Emperor in Delhi from the very beginning of their existence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Hyderabad remained a cohesive autocratic dynastic state, whereas the Marathas federated into distinct regional houses. Statement 2 is incorrect: Neither state initially rejected Mughal sovereignty outright; Nizam-ul-Mulk operated nominally under Mughal farmans and titles while maintaining de facto independence, and the Marathas also frequently used imperial sanctions and claimed legitimacy through Mughal administrative frameworks until much later. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History]
